purpose: Define the complete, compilable, verbatim shape and observable serde contract of monokl's dependency/export/JSX/language-data type cluster -- DependencyRecord, DependencyBinding, BindingKind, DependencyTarget, RustPathAnchor, ExportRecord, JsxAttribute, JsxElementEntry, LangData (plus its two methods), and the five per-language data structs (TsData, RustData, PythonData, GoData, JavaData) -- per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 4 (lines 312-452), so a developer implementing types.rs, or any downstream analyzer constructing these values, never has to guess a variant, field, serde tag strategy, or rename. This cluster is where two structurally different serde enum-tagging strategies coexist (DependencyTarget's internally-tagged `tag = "kind"`, which flattens each variant's fields into the same JSON object as the tag, versus LangData's adjacently-tagged `tag = "language", content = "data"`, which keeps the tag and the variant's payload in two separate keys) and where some #[serde(rename = ...)] overrides are functionally necessary to produce the intended JSON string (RustPathAnchor::Selff -> "self"; LangData::Ts -> "typescript") while others are redundant with what the enclosing rename_all = "camelCase" would already produce on its own -- precision an implementer would otherwise have to reverse-engineer from serde's own transform rules rather than read directly.
scope: DependencyRecord (3 fields), DependencyBinding (3 fields), BindingKind (5 variants), DependencyTarget (an internally-tagged, #[non_exhaustive] 3-variant enum), RustPathAnchor (a #[non_exhaustive] 4-variant enum with one functionally necessary rename), ExportRecord (3 fields), JsxAttribute (4 fields), JsxElementEntry (4 fields), LangData (an adjacently-tagged, #[non_exhaustive] 5-variant enum plus its ts()/jsx_elements() methods), TsData (3 fields, the only one of the five per-language data structs with real content), and RustData/PythonData/GoData/JavaData (four structurally identical empty placeholder structs) -- all verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:312-452, including the "Post-research correction" note at lines 397-400 explaining why Go/Java replace an earlier CSharp variant. docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md independently restates RustPathAnchor (03-multi-language-platform.md:2405-2417), DependencyTarget (2419-2442), and LangData plus its ts()/jsx_elements() methods (2381-2403) in its own 'types added' changelog block, each confirmed semantically identical to the canonical source -- differing only in single-line-vs-multi-line attribute formatting, no drift found. It locks each type's exact field/variant order, derive list, and serde attributes; the two distinct enum-tagging JSON shapes these types produce; which #[serde(rename = ...)] overrides are necessary versus redundant; and the observable deserialize consequences of #[non_exhaustive] (a Rust-level match-exhaustiveness attribute with no effect on serde's generated (de)serialize code) versus the presence or absence of #[serde(default)] on Vec-typed fields, which -- unlike Option-typed fields -- do not get implicit missing-key leniency from serde's derive macro without that attribute.
non_goals: All other Section 4 types not in this cluster -- SymbolKind/Visibility/SymbolEntry (locked in SPEC-003) and CodeBlock/RankedBlock/ParentContext/Diagnostic/DiagnosticKind/SearchOptions/SearchLimits/Language/SearchResponse/SymbolsResult/DependentsResult/LineHit/TsconfigMode/WorkspaceOptions/ExtractRequest (a separate, later track).

Which language construct a given analyzer maps to which DependencyTarget variant, RustPathAnchor variant, or BindingKind variant -- an analyzer-implementation-track decision, not locked here beyond the variants' existence and shape.
TsData/RustData/PythonData/GoData/JavaData's population semantics -- which analyzer sets which field, and when -- owned by each language analyzer's own implementation track.

Whether GoData/JavaData (or PythonData) gain real fields once their analyzers land -- that is those future analyzer tracks' job; this track locks only their current, empty shape and the documented reason they're empty today.

Resolving whether DependencyTarget::Namespace should eventually be removed or repurposed, and whether the not-yet-built generic tree-sitter fallback-tier C# analyzer decided in 05-research-and-decisions.md §10 will construct Namespace values once implemented -- this track documents the variant as unused in the corpus's current verbatim code (AC-007) without deciding either question.

Whether any document in the corpus beyond 01-core-architecture.md and 03-multi-language-platform.md independently restates these types -- this track checked and confirms no drift between those two (see scope), but does not claim to have checked every other document in docs/spec/*.md for a further restatement.

api_surface.name: LangData::ts
api_surface.description: 01-core-architecture.md:419-421. Returns Some(&TsData) only when self is the Ts variant; None for every other variant (Rust, Python, Go, Java).

api_surface.name: LangData::jsx_elements
api_surface.description: 01-core-architecture.md:422-424. Delegates to ts(): returns the TsData's jsx_elements slice when self is the Ts variant, or an empty slice for every other variant. Never panics; always returns a valid (possibly empty) reference -- see AC-016.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: DependencyRecord (01-core-architecture.md:314-319) compiles with exactly 3 fields in this order: line: usize, bindings: Vec<DependencyBinding>, target: DependencyTarget. It carries exactly two attribute lines (#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)], #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]) -- no Copy/PartialEq/Eq. Only bindings carries a field-level attribute: #[serde(default)] with no skip_serializing_if (line 316-317); line and target carry no field-level attributes and are required -- a JSON object omitting either "line" or "target" fails to deserialize with a missing-field error naming that field, the same consequence DependencyBinding's three required fields produce (AC-002). Consequence for bindings: a DependencyRecord whose bindings vec is empty still serializes the key ("bindings":[]), unlike a skip_serializing_if field which would omit it; on deserialize, an object omitting the "bindings" key entirely succeeds, defaulting to an empty vec via that explicit #[serde(default)] -- and, unlike an Option-typed field (where #[serde(default)] is redundant with the type's own implicit missing-key leniency, per SPEC-003 AC-005), this attribute is NOT redundant here: Vec<T> receives no implicit leniency from serde's derive macro, so without #[serde(default)] a missing "bindings" key would fail with a missing-field error instead. Contrast with JsxElementEntry.attributes (AC-011), a Vec field with no such attribute.

DependencyBinding (01-core-architecture.md:323-327) compiles with exactly 3 fields in this order: imported: String, local: String, kind: BindingKind. Two attribute lines, identical structure to AC-001 (Debug/Clone/Serialize/Deserialize, rename_all camelCase); no field-level attributes on any of the 3 fields, so all three are required on deserialize (a JSON object omitting any of "imported"/"local"/"kind" fails with a missing-field error naming that field).

BindingKind (01-core-architecture.md:331-337) compiles with exactly these 5 variants, in this order: Named, Default, Namespace, Glob, NamespaceWide. Two attribute lines: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] (Copy/PartialEq/Eq present, matching SymbolKind's and Visibility's pattern from SPEC-003, since this is a fieldless enum) and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] -- no #[non_exhaustive].

BindingKind's camelCase JSON forms are exactly: Named->"named", Default->"default", Namespace->"namespace", Glob->"glob", NamespaceWide->"namespaceWide". For NamespaceWide, serde's variant-level camelCase rule (lowercase only the leading character, per SPEC-003 AC-002's established finding) already produces the fully correct camelCase spelling here, because Rust's PascalCase variant-naming convention marks NamespaceWide's internal word boundary via capitalization (Namespace + Wide) rather than via an underscore -- unlike a snake_case struct field name, no further restructuring is needed to reach "namespaceWide".

DependencyTarget (01-core-architecture.md:342-358) is an internally tagged enum: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] (no Copy/PartialEq/Eq), #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind")], #[non_exhaustive], with exactly 3 variants in this order: File { specifier: String, resolved: Option<Utf8PathBuf>, is_relative: bool }, RustPath { segments: Vec<String>, anchor: RustPathAnchor, resolved: Option<Utf8PathBuf> }, Namespace { segments: Vec<String>, is_static: bool, alias: Option<String> }. Internal tagging means each variant's own fields are flattened directly into the same JSON object as the "kind" tag key, not nested under a separate variant-name key. The enum-level #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] renames only the three variant tag values -- File->"file", RustPath->"rustPath", Namespace->"namespace" -- it does NOT rename the fields of these struct-shaped variants: renaming variant fields requires the separate rename_all_fields attribute, which this enum does not carry. Consequently File's actual wire shape is {"kind":"file","specifier":...,"resolved":...,"is_relative":...} (the field key stays snake_case, not "isRelative"), and Namespace's is {"kind":"namespace","segments":...,"is_static":...,"alias":...} -- struct-variant field names keep their Rust snake_case spelling regardless of the container-level camelCase attribute, an asymmetry with every plain struct in this cluster (AC-001, AC-009, AC-010, AC-011, AC-017), where the same rename_all attribute genuinely does camelCase the fields since there is no variant-tag/field distinction to complicate it there. A JSON object using "isRelative" instead of "is_relative" (or "isStatic" instead of "is_static") fails to deserialize with a missing-field error naming the snake_case field. #[non_exhaustive] here is a Rust-compiler-level attribute controlling exhaustive match/construct checking for code outside this crate; it has no effect on serde's generated (de)serialize behavior -- see AC-006.

DependencyTarget carries no #[serde(other)] fallback and #[non_exhaustive] (AC-005) does not introduce one -- deserializing a JSON object whose "kind" value does not exactly match "file", "rustPath", or "namespace" fails with a serde unknown-variant error, identically to how it would fail if the enum were not marked #[non_exhaustive]. Within each variant, all fields are required except File.resolved and RustPath.resolved and Namespace.alias, which are Option-typed with no field-level serde attribute of their own -- per SPEC-003 AC-005's established finding, each still deserializes leniently to None on a missing or explicitly-null key, since that leniency comes from Option<T>'s own Deserialize implementation, not from a #[serde(default)] attribute this struct does not carry.

DependencyTarget::Namespace (AC-005) is confirmed spec residue from a dropped roadmap item: docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md documents it (Part 3 finding #20) as present because an earlier C# roadmap target used it, and docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md §6 records that C# was dropped from the bespoke Go/Java-tier language roadmap specifically. C# is not absent from the corpus, however: 05-research-and-decisions.md §10 separately adopts a generic tree-sitter fallback tier whose launch set explicitly includes C#, work that document's own summary characterizes as decided but not yet built. No analyzer in 01-core-architecture.md's or 03-multi-language-platform.md's verbatim code constructs a DependencyTarget::Namespace value today -- a corpus-wide search for the literal string "DependencyTarget::Namespace" across docs/spec/*.md returns exactly three hits, none of them a construction site: two pattern-match arms returning None (01-core-architecture.md:2040, 03-multi-language-platform.md:1889) and one prose occurrence inside the finding #20 write-up itself (07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md:130). The two enum declarations (01-core-architecture.md:353, 03-multi-language-platform.md:2436) read "Namespace {", not the qualified path, so they are not hits of that literal search. 03-multi-language-platform.md additionally shows the variant being consumed, not constructed: line 1979 records that the dependency_target_resolved helper "returns None for Namespace (C# uses these but no resolver exists yet)", and line 1155 records that a second helper, dependency_target_matches, "handles File/RustPath/Namespace targets" -- routing Namespace through the same matching path as File/RustPath rather than special-casing it as an error. Whether the not-yet-built §10 fallback-tier C# analyzer will construct one once implemented is undetermined and explicitly out of scope for this track (see non_goals) -- this criterion asserts only the current, verbatim-code state, not a claim about that future analyzer's eventual behavior. This is cosmetic residue in the code that exists today, not a functional defect: the variant compiles and round-trips through serde normally (AC-005, AC-006); nothing about its presence breaks File or RustPath handling.

RustPathAnchor (01-core-architecture.md:363-369) is #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] (no Copy/PartialEq/Eq, since Extern(String) carries a payload), #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], #[non_exhaustive], with exactly 4 variants in this order: Crate, Super, Selff (the Rust identifier is spelled with two f's -- self is a reserved keyword and cannot name an enum variant), Extern(String). Crate, Super, and Extern receive the default camelCase transform with no override, producing tag values "crate", "super", and "extern" respectively (Extern's associated String is carried as the tagged value's content, not flattened as a named field, since this is an externally-tagged enum by default -- no tag/content attributes are present on this enum, unlike DependencyTarget and LangData). Selff alone carries an explicit #[serde(rename = "self")] (line 366), and this override is functionally necessary, not merely stylistic: without it, serde's default camelCase transform of the identifier "Selff" would lowercase only its leading character, producing "selff" -- not "self" -- so the explicit rename is what makes the JSON value correctly read "self" rather than the Rust-identifier-workaround spelling leaking into the wire format.

ExportRecord (01-core-architecture.md:373-377) compiles with exactly 3 fields in this order: name: String, line: usize, re_export: bool. Exactly two attribute lines, #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] (no Copy/PartialEq/Eq) and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]; no field-level attributes; all three fields are required on deserialize: a JSON object omitting any of "name"/"line"/"reExport" fails to deserialize with a missing-field error naming that field. Under rename_all = "camelCase", re_export's JSON key is reExport; name and line are unchanged.

JsxAttribute (01-core-architecture.md:381-386) compiles with exactly 4 fields in this order: name: String, string_value: Option<String>, is_expression: bool, is_spread: bool. Exactly two attribute lines, #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] (no Copy/PartialEq/Eq) and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]; no field-level attributes on any of the 4 fields. name/is_expression/is_spread are required on deserialize: a JSON object omitting any of "name"/"isExpression"/"isSpread" fails to deserialize with a missing-field error naming that field. string_value, despite carrying no #[serde(default)] or skip_serializing_if, still deserializes leniently to None on a missing or explicitly-null "stringValue" key -- the same Option<T>-implicit-leniency pattern established in SPEC-003 AC-005/AC-010, here appearing on a field with zero serde attributes at all rather than the full #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)] pairing SymbolEntry's optional fields carry. On serialize, a None string_value emits its key with a JSON null value (no skip_serializing_if to omit it) -- the same always-present-key-when-unset pattern as SymbolEntry.signature (SPEC-003 AC-005), not the omit-key-when-unset pattern SymbolEntry's other optional fields use. Under rename_all = "camelCase": string_value -> stringValue, is_expression -> isExpression, is_spread -> isSpread.

JsxElementEntry (01-core-architecture.md:390-395) compiles with exactly 4 fields in this order: name: String, is_html: bool, line: usize, attributes: Vec<JsxAttribute>. Exactly two attribute lines, #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] (no Copy/PartialEq/Eq) and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]; no field-level attributes on any of the 4 fields -- notably, unlike DependencyRecord.bindings (AC-001), attributes carries no #[serde(default)]. Because Vec<T> receives no implicit missing-key leniency from serde's derive macro (that leniency is specific to Option<T>, per AC-006/AC-010), all 4 fields including attributes are required on deserialize: a JSON object omitting "attributes" fails with a missing-field error, exactly like omitting "name", "isHtml", or "line" would. Under rename_all = "camelCase": is_html -> isHtml.

LangData (01-core-architecture.md:402-416) is an adjacently tagged enum: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] (no Copy/PartialEq/Eq), #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "language", content = "data")], #[non_exhaustive], with exactly 5 variants in this order: Ts(TsData), Rust(RustData), Python(PythonData), Go(GoData), Java(JavaData). Adjacent tagging keeps the tag and the variant's payload in two separate keys of the same object -- e.g. the Ts variant serializes as {"language":"typescript","data":{...TsData's own fields...}} -- a structurally different JSON shape from DependencyTarget's internal tagging (AC-005), which flattens variant fields directly alongside the tag key with no separate content wrapper. Each variant carries its own explicit #[serde(rename = ...)] tag value: Ts->"typescript", Rust->"rust", Python->"python", Go->"go", Java->"java".

Of LangData's 5 explicit #[serde(rename = ...)] tag values (AC-012), exactly one is functionally necessary: Ts's rename to "typescript" changes the tag value from what the enclosing rename_all = "camelCase" would otherwise produce by default (lowercasing Ts's leading character alone would give "ts", not "typescript") -- the override is doing real work. The remaining four renames (Rust->"rust", Python->"python", Go->"go", Java->"java") are redundant with what the default camelCase transform would already produce for these single-word, already-lowercase-after-leading-character variant names -- present in the source but not changing any observable behavior versus omitting them. This mirrors the necessary-vs-redundant pattern in RustPathAnchor's renames (AC-008), where Selff's rename is necessary and Crate/Super/Extern's default transform already suffices.

LangData carries no #[serde(other)] fallback and #[non_exhaustive] does not introduce one (same distinction as AC-006). Deserializing a JSON object whose "language" value does not exactly match one of the 5 tag values in AC-012 fails with a serde unknown-variant error. Deserializing a well-formed "language" tag whose paired "data" object does not match that variant's inner struct shape (AC-017, AC-018) fails according to that inner struct's own deserialize contract -- e.g. a "language":"typescript" object whose "data" value holds a type-mismatched field (a non-array "jsxElements", say) fails per AC-017's own per-field contract, not with a LangData-specific error. An unrecognized extra key inside that "data" object, by contrast, does not fail -- it is silently discarded per AC-019, the same as anywhere else in this cluster.

The Post-research correction note at 01-core-architecture.md:397-400 states Go and Java replace an earlier CSharp variant on LangData, reflecting a language-roadmap decision to drop C# in favor of Go and Java (docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md §6), and that GoData and JavaData are empty placeholders today, identical in shape to PythonData -- populated once those analyzers land. This is forward-looking, documented scope, not an oversight: LangData's own #[non_exhaustive] attribute (AC-012) means adding further LangData variants for additional languages does not require this spec to be revised for external-crate exhaustive-match compatibility on LangData itself. That protection is enum-level only and does not extend to GoData/JavaData's own fields -- none of the four per-language data structs (AC-018) carries #[non_exhaustive] on its own struct declaration, so adding real fields to GoData or JavaData later is a separate compatibility question this track does not resolve, not one LangData's attribute already covers.

LangData::ts(&self) -> Option<&TsData> (01-core-architecture.md:419-421) returns Some(&TsData) if and only if self is the Ts variant, and None for every one of the other 4 variants (Rust, Python, Go, Java) -- never panics regardless of which variant self holds. LangData::jsx_elements(&self) -> &[JsxElementEntry] (01-core-architecture.md:422-424) is defined as self.ts().map_or(&[], |ts| ts.jsx_elements.as_slice()): it returns TsData.jsx_elements as a slice when self is Ts, and an empty slice for every other variant -- also never panics. Both methods are pure, infallible reads with no side effects and no error conditions, verifiable directly from the bodies quoted above: neither contains a panic-capable operation (no indexing, unwrap, or arithmetic that could overflow) on any LangData variant.

TsData (01-core-architecture.md:427-436) is the only one of the 5 per-language data structs (AC-018) with real fields: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)], #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], exactly 3 fields in this order -- jsx_elements: Vec<JsxElementEntry> [#[serde(default)], no skip_serializing_if], type_only_imports: Vec<String> [#[serde(default)], no skip_serializing_if], unresolved_aliases: Vec<String> [#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]]. Of these three Vec fields, only unresolved_aliases omits its JSON key when empty; jsx_elements and type_only_imports both always serialize their key even when the vec is empty ("jsxElements":[], "typeOnlyImports":[]), the same always-present pattern as DependencyRecord.bindings (AC-001) -- all three fields deserialize leniently (defaulting to an empty vec) on a missing key, since all three carry the explicit #[serde(default)] that Vec<T> fields require for that leniency (AC-001, AC-011). TsData::default() (via the derived Default impl) produces all three fields as empty vecs.

RustData, PythonData, GoData, and JavaData (01-core-architecture.md:438-452) are four structurally identical, field-less structs: pub struct XData {} for each, all sharing #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)] and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] (the rename_all attribute is vacuous for a field-less struct -- present for consistency with the cluster's other types, not because it changes any observable behavior). Each serializes as an empty JSON object ({}) and deserializes successfully from {}; each XData::default() (via the derived Default impl) is simply XData {}.

None of this cluster's 10 struct/enum types (DependencyRecord, DependencyBinding, BindingKind, DependencyTarget, RustPathAnchor, ExportRecord, JsxAttribute, JsxElementEntry, LangData, TsData) or the 4 empty per-language data structs (AC-018) carries #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] anywhere in their declarations (01-core-architecture.md:312-452). A JSON object with an extra, unrecognized key alongside otherwise-valid content deserializes successfully for every one of these 14 types, silently discarding the unrecognized key -- it does not error, and does not populate any field from it. This holds identically for the two tagged enums (DependencyTarget, LangData): an extra key alongside a valid "kind"/"language" tag and its required payload fields is likewise accepted and discarded, not rejected.

linked_research: docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:312-452 (Section 4 types.rs verbatim -- the primary source for every type and method in this track; the "Post-research correction" note at lines 397-400); docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md:2405-2417 (independent restatement of RustPathAnchor), :2419-2442 (DependencyTarget), :2381-2403 (LangData plus its two methods) -- all confirmed identical to the canonical source; :1889 (a DependencyTarget::Namespace pattern-match arm), :1979 and :1155 (Namespace-consuming, not constructing, helper code), all cited for AC-007; docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md (Part 3 finding #20, DependencyTarget::Namespace as C#-roadmap residue); docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md §6 (the C#-dropped-from-the-Go/Java-tier decision) and §10 (the generic tree-sitter fallback tier's launch set, which reintroduces C#, cited for AC-007's corrected scoping); .claude/specs/SPEC-003.json (AC-002, AC-005, AC-010's established serde-semantics findings -- variant-level vs. field-level camelCase transform rules, Option<T>'s implicit missing-key deserialize leniency -- re-applied and, where the underlying mechanism differs, explicitly contrasted rather than assumed to generalize, e.g. AC-001/AC-011's Vec<T>-does-not-share-that-leniency finding).
revision_note:
Fourth draft, after canon-exit-gate's second pass (retry 2, fail on one narrow finding out of 19 criteria, 18 confirmed clean via live compiled-toolchain re-derivation): AC-007's consumed-not-constructed clause attributed the line-1979 quote to dependency_target_matches, but that quote's actual source is a different, similarly-named helper, dependency_target_resolved -- dependency_target_matches is the function at line 1155, described differently there. Fixed to attribute each quote to its correct helper.

Third draft, after canon-exit-gate's first pass (retry 1, fail). The gate found the single most consequential defect in this track: AC-005 claimed DependencyTarget's struct-variant fields (is_relative, is_static) get camelCase-renamed by the enum's container-level #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] -- false. That attribute renames only the variant tag values; renaming struct-variant fields requires the separate rename_all_fields attribute, which this enum does not carry, so the real wire keys stay snake_case (is_relative, is_static). This is exactly the struct-vs-enum unwarranted-generalization error the revision_note's prior draft claimed to have proactively guarded against (correctly, for Vec-vs-Option) and missed here -- fixed by restating the actual wire shape and explaining why the container-level attribute doesn't reach into struct-variant fields the way it does for a plain struct. The gate also found: AC-007's corpus-wide-grep citation (added in the prior round to fix an earlier overclaim) itself misdescribed its own results -- it credited the enum declaration as a hit when the declaration doesn't match the literal string searched, and omitted a real third hit at 07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md:130 -- fixed to state the grep result exactly as it reproduces, plus added the consumed-not-constructed context from 03-multi-language-platform.md:1979/:1155. The 03-multi-language-platform.md cross-check citation pointed at the wrong line range (2400-2436, which opens mid-LangData-impl and truncates DependencyTarget) and omitted a real, confirmed-identical LangData restatement at 2381-2403 -- both fixed with the correct ranges. Six of eighteen criteria (AC-005, AC-008 through AC-012) said 'two attribute lines' without naming the derive list, while scope claims this track locks derive lists explicitly and several sibling criteria (AC-001, AC-003) do name theirs -- fixed by stating each type's derive list explicitly. A new criterion (AC-019) added stating that no type in the cluster carries #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], an observable serde behavior (unrecognized keys silently discarded cluster-wide) the prior drafts never asserted despite the spec's stated purpose of locking 'the complete... observable serde contract'.

Second draft, after canon-verifier/canon-auditor's first review round. canon-verifier found 17 of 18 criteria and both api_surface methods cleanly supported, catching one real overclaim: AC-015 attributed GoData/JavaData's future field-growth compatibility to LangData's own #[non_exhaustive] attribute, conflating an enum-level exhaustive-match protection with a struct-level field-growth concern the four per-language data structs' own (non-#[non_exhaustive]) declarations don't actually have -- fixed to state the two as separate, unresolved questions. canon-auditor found: AC-007's negative claim ('no analyzer... planned... constructs Namespace') didn't reconcile with 05-research-and-decisions.md §10, which reintroduces C# (the variant's original motivating language) as a decided fallback-tier launch-set target in the same document -- fixed to scope the claim to the current verbatim code only, not to planned-but-unbuilt work, with a corpus-wide-grep citation added matching this project's established practice for negative claims; the corresponding non_goal updated to match. Uneven is_error_case coverage across the required-field cluster: AC-001 stated no missing-field consequence for DependencyRecord's line/target (added, tagged true); AC-002 stated the consequence but was mistagged false (retagged true); AC-009/AC-010 stated only the label 'required' without the observable consequence (both extended and retagged true). AC-016's 'intentional, not an omission' clause asserted a fact about this document's own authorial intent rather than LangData's observable behavior -- replaced with a verifiable panic-freedom argument. A non_goals internal inconsistency ('outside the two locations this spec cites' with only one location actually named) fixed by citing the confirmed 03-multi-language-platform.md restatement of DependencyTarget/RustPathAnchor the auditor found and verified identical -- folded into scope and linked_research as a real cross-check per SPEC-003's established precedent, rather than left as an unchecked disclaimer.

First draft. Drafted directly against primary source (01-core-architecture.md:312-452) with SPEC-001/SPEC-003/SPEC-004's established lessons applied proactively rather than discovered via a failed gate round: independently re-derived each serde-attribute's actual behavioral consequence rather than assuming a pattern found once (Option<T>'s implicit deserialize leniency, SPEC-003 AC-005) generalizes to a structurally different type (Vec<T> does not share it, confirmed via serde's own documented derive-macro special-casing, which is specific to Option-typed fields) rather than asserting it uniformly; distinguished #[non_exhaustive] (a Rust match-exhaustiveness attribute) from any effect on serde-generated (de)serialize code (it has none) at both of this cluster's #[non_exhaustive] enums (DependencyTarget, LangData) rather than stating it once and assuming the reader generalizes; and worked out, rather than assumed, which of RustPathAnchor's and LangData's explicit #[serde(rename = ...)] overrides are functionally necessary (change the JSON value from what the default transform would produce) versus redundant (restate what the default transform already produces) by computing the default transform for each variant name by hand before comparing it to the explicit rename.
reasoning: This track's central technical risk, identified before drafting rather than discovered via correction: two different serde enum-tagging strategies (DependencyTarget's internal tag="kind" with no content key, LangData's adjacent tag="language"+content="data") coexist in the same small cluster, and it would be easy to describe one in terms that accidentally also describe the other, or to state a JSON shape for one that's actually the other's shape. Verified each independently against the verbatim source (lines 342 and 402 respectively) and stated their structural difference explicitly in both AC-005 and AC-012 rather than relying on the reader to infer it from two separately-read code blocks. Also treated Vec<T> and Option<T>'s field-attribute behavior as genuinely distinct questions rather than assuming SPEC-003's Option<T> finding transfers -- this is exactly the kind of unwarranted generalization that produced real, gate-caught defects in SPEC-003's earlier rounds (the false claim that a missing 'signature' key fails to deserialize), so this draft computed Vec<T>'s actual behavior (no implicit leniency; #[serde(default)] is load-bearing, not redundant) from first principles rather than assuming symmetry with the already-verified Option<T> case. Did not independently re-run serde/serde_json against a live toolchain for this draft (matching this project's now-established practice of flagging when a claim rests on documented library semantics rather than fresh empirical reproduction) -- the Vec<T>-vs-Option<T> distinction, the internal-vs-adjacent tagging JSON shapes, and the necessary-vs-redundant rename analysis all rest on serde's publicly documented, stable derive-macro behavior, but a review pass with toolchain access should still verify AC-001, AC-006, AC-011, and AC-014's specific claimed error messages/shapes empirically, consistent with the error class that has recurred across every behavioral track in this project so far.
